title: A decision you can inspect
subtitle: Customer presentation · January forecasts, actuals, and accuracy together
narration: Welcome to Wind Decision Replay. This pilot helps an electricity buying team inspect the wind forecast available for a historical next day purchasing decision and measure its performance against recorded generation. Forecasts, actuals, accuracy cards, and revision evidence are visible immediately when the data loads. There is no reveal or unlock step. The starting example is the fifteenth of January twenty twenty six at nine in the morning, for delivery on the sixteenth. The dashboard reads the permitted Elexon APIs and identifies the source and retrieval status. We will explore the customer workflow, then review the architecture and its checks. This walkthrough uses actual application captures and disclosed synthetic narration.

title: Choose the historical decision
subtitle: Customer presentation · Publication eligibility remains fixed at the decision cutoff
narration: The controls specify a decision date and a cutoff in London time. Nine o'clock is a configurable demonstration assumption, rather than a universal market deadline. For every delivery hour, the backend selects the latest forecast published at or before the selected checkpoint. An update released later cannot enter an earlier decision, even when the source data is freshly retrieved today. The publication timeline lets us inspect earlier eligible revisions. Some early publications cover fewer next day hours, and that difference is reported. Actual generation remains clearly retrospective: it is visible to evaluate this historical decision, not presented as information that the buyer possessed in advance.

title: Actuals and accuracy immediately
subtitle: Customer presentation · Complete hourly comparisons without an extra click
narration: The recorded generation line and error measures appear alongside the forecast as soon as the request completes. Forecasts are hourly, while the source actuals are half hourly. Two complete half hours are averaged to make one comparable hourly observation. In the preserved reference example, the midnight forecast was seven thousand three hundred and ninety eight megawatts and the recorded hourly average was seven thousand three hundred and thirty five point five. The positive error was sixty two point five megawatts. Positive means wind was overforecast. This measures a generation mismatch. The permitted datasets contain neither customer demand nor the client's contracted portfolio, so the dashboard does not claim to calculate the exact electricity they should buy.

title: Inspect the revision evidence
subtitle: Customer presentation · Compare both forecasts on identical delivery hours
narration: A newer forecast does not automatically improve every error measure. In the preserved example, selected mean absolute error was seven hundred and eighty two point seven five megawatts, compared with seven hundred and thirty six point two nine for the previous revisions. That is six point three percent higher error across the same twenty four hours. Eight hours improved and sixteen worsened. Yet positive overforecast energy was lower: around thirteen thousand six hundred and seventeen megawatt hours, compared with fourteen thousand five hundred and forty eight. These statistics answer different questions. The comparison exposes its common sample size. This retrospective case is evidence to inspect, not a rule that older forecasts should always be preferred.

title: Refresh the source and review January
subtitle: Customer presentation · Real API requests, visible freshness, and the full month
narration: The refresh control makes a new request to Elexon's real historical APIs. The status identifies a successful API response, reuse of the short lived API cache, or an explicitly labelled fallback after upstream failure. Its retrieval timestamp describes when the records were obtained, not when a forecast was originally published. January remains the scope after refresh. The monthly view applies the same cutoff to every January decision and reports accuracy and coverage together. At midnight, some forecasts do not cover all delivery hours, so those observations remain missing. Every revision comparison uses identical hours. A failed refresh preserves last good data and reports the failure instead of silently claiming fresh results.

title: One dataset for every view
subtitle: Technical review · React, FastAPI, real API retrieval, and one dataset epoch
narration: The architecture separates source retrieval, analysis, and presentation. A Python provider requests the two permitted Elexon datasets and normalizes their records. FastAPI performs publication selection and accuracy calculations. React and TypeScript display the results and the source status. The dashboard endpoint returns the selected decision, January analysis, metadata, and freshness from one dataset epoch, preventing panels from mixing independently refreshed versions. Docker builds the frontend and packages it with the Python application. Vercel serves the frontend and runs the same ASGI application as a Python function. A bundled snapshot is retained only for an explicitly identified upstream failure, rather than as the application's ordinary data source.

title: Cache honestly and preserve provenance
subtitle: Technical review · A 300 second instance cache and explicit failure behaviour
narration: The provider fetches the fixed historical source windows from Elexon, preserving target times and publication times. It caches a successful normalized dataset in process memory for three hundred seconds. Each Vercel instance owns its own cache, so a cold instance performs its own request. The manual refresh endpoint bypasses that interval. Successful retrieval records the source URLs, attempt time, and retrieval time. A failed refresh retains the last good dataset, its original successful retrieval time, and an explicit stale error status. If no successful API data exists, an upstream failure can use the bundled snapshot with its original metadata and a fallback label. It must never masquerade as a fresh API result.

title: Keep the analysis auditable
subtitle: Technical review · Historical eligibility, complete actuals, and shared cohorts
narration: Fresh retrieval does not change the information boundary of a historical decision. Publication time must still be at or before its selected cutoff, independently for each target hour. The previous forecast is the previous distinct eligible publication for that target. Both actual half hours are required before averaging their megawatt values. Missing observations remain unavailable, while zero remains a valid measurement. Headline accuracy uses all complete forecast and actual matches. Revision comparisons use the common hours containing both revisions and the actual. Positive hourly errors multiplied by one hour give the overforecast energy in megawatt hours. January decision dates imply delivery from the second of January through the first of February; source retrieval does not widen the product scope.

title: Verify visibility and refresh semantics
subtitle: Technical review · Domain tests, provider failures, and frontend interactions
narration: The tests cover the behaviours that would undermine the analysis if they were wrong. Domain checks exclude future publications, include an exact cutoff, retain valid zeroes, require complete actual hours, and verify the error formulas. A partial coverage regression prevents different samples from reversing the apparent revision result. Provider tests exercise real request construction, cache reuse, forced refresh, and failure handling without depending on an external service during the test run. Frontend interactions check that actuals and accuracy are immediately available and that refresh state is visible. The continuous integration workflow runs Python tests, frontend interaction tests, TypeScript checks, and the production build. The final source and production checks must also confirm that the deployed app reaches the real Elexon endpoints.

title: Deliver a reviewable historical pilot
subtitle: Technical review · Reproducible execution, visible freshness, and clear limits
narration: The repository includes React, Python, the API provider, analysis tests, Docker setup, and deployment configuration. The README documents the directory structure, run commands, source rules, cache behaviour, failure handling, and AI assistance. The unified dashboard response keeps every view on one dataset epoch, while CSV export makes selected evidence inspectable. Manual refresh retrieves the historical records again; it does not turn this January pilot into a current trading dashboard. Cache memory is disposable and local to a server instance, a deliberate simplification for this bounded demonstration. Before handoff, verify the public application without a login, inspect the refresh status, and watch the regenerated local video. The video remains local at the candidate's request, and no submission form is sent automatically.
